The Balaramapuram Kasavu Project will be inaugurated by Keralam Chief Minister V D Satheesan at Kanakakkunnu Palace at 3.30 PM. Union Minister of State Suresh […]
item.content:encoded:
A unique initiative celebrating India’s traditional handloom heritage is set to be launched in Thiruvananthapuram this evening, with a 6,000-foot-long kasavu textile created by around 2,500 weavers from Kerala’s Balaramapuram. The Balaramapuram Kasavu Project will be inaugurated by Keralam Chief Minister V D Satheesan at Kanakakkunnu Palace at 3.30 PM. Union Minister of State Suresh Gopi will attend as the chief guest.
 
The project seeks to bring national and international attention to India’s traditional weaving communities, while highlighting the craftsmanship and cultural legacy of Keralam’s handloom sector. The 6,000-foot-long textile, curated in collaboration with Balaramapuram weavers, will showcase the generations-old weaving tradition through an artistic presentation. Balaramapuram handloom sarees and fine cotton fabrics, known for their distinctive gold kasavu borders, were the first handloom products from Keralam to receive a Geographical Indication tag.

item.content:encoded:
Around 26,000 domestic birds are being culled today within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentres in Alappuzha district of Keralam, following a confirmed outbreak of avian influenza. The culling operation is underway across three Grama Panchayats under the joint supervision of the Animal Husbandry and Health departments. 

Avian influenza was confirmed in quails, ducks and chickens at two farms in Alappuzha district of Keralam. Samples tested at the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal returned positive for the virus. Six Rapid Response Teams have been deployed to carry out the culling drive, with two additional teams kept on reserve. A 10-kilometre radius around the affected farms has been declared a surveillance zone.

item.title: India participates as Guest of Honour in UAE’s National Festival of Tolerance and Coexistence
item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: The 8th edition of UAE’s National Festival of Tolerance and Coexistence opened at Umm Al Emarat Park in Abu Dhabi on Friday, with India participating as the Country Guest of Honour. The three-day festival brings together more than 22 countries through cultural performances, community activities and family-oriented programmes and was inaugurated by Sheikh Nahayan […]
item.content:encoded:
The 8th edition of UAE’s National Festival of Tolerance and Coexistence opened at Umm Al Emarat Park in Abu Dhabi on Friday, with India participating as the Country Guest of Honour. The three-day festival brings together more than 22 countries through cultural performances, community activities and family-oriented programmes and was inaugurated by Sheikh Nahayan Mabarak Al Nahayan, UAE’s Minister of Tolerance & Coexistence.
 
Highlighting the longstanding ties between India and the UAE, Sheikh Nahayan said the friendship rooted in centuries of trade, travel and cultural exchanges across the Arabian Sea, had evolved into a dynamic partnership spanning education, technology and several other fields. He also acknowledged the Indian community’s significant contributions to the UAE’s development and its social and cultural life.
 
Indian Ambassador to the UAE Dr. Deepak Mittal said India’s designation as Guest of Honour reflected the special place the India held in the hearts of the UAE’s people. He said the festival celebrates coexistence as a lived experience, built through shared music, food, stories and friendships, and India’s participation embodies this spirit of cultural confluence.
 
Being held from 13-15 November, the annual festival marks the International Day for Tolerance and seeks to promote tolerance, peaceful coexistence, human fraternity and respect for cultural diversity. This year’s edition is being held under the theme ‘Growing in Unity’. It also celebrates the legacy of UAE’s Founding Father, Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, in building an inclusive and cohesive society.
 
India’s designation as Country Guest of Honour will be marked by a series of cultural performances across all three days of the festival, showcasing the country’s diverse artistic traditions. The Indian programme opened on Friday with a dance performance titled ‘Koli Fishermen of Bombay: Guardians of Sustainability, Tolerance and Brotherhood’, that highlighted the cultural traditions and community life of Mumbai’s fishing community.
 
An India Pavilion at the festival showcases the country’s rich heritage through displays of traditional crafts, jewellery and paintings, alongside interactive activities like know India quiz, offering visitors an opportunity to explore India’s culture and diversity.
 
Today, the festival will feature a Kerala Cultural Showcase, presented by the World Malayalee Council Abu Dhabi. The Indian participation will culminate on Sunday with a special performance titled ‘Incredible India – A Cultural Extravaganza’, bringing together a showcase of the country’s cultural diversity.<>

item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: India Post has entered into a bilateral agreement with the Travancore Devaswom Board to set up a round-the-clock special ‘Swami Prasadam’ booking counter at Sabarimala temple in Keralam ahead of the upcoming Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season. The initiative aims to facilitate the delivery of sacred Swami Prasadam, including Aravana Payasam, to devotees at their doorsteps through […]
item.content:encoded:
India Post has entered into a bilateral agreement with the Travancore Devaswom Board to set up a round-the-clock special ‘Swami Prasadam’ booking counter at Sabarimala temple in Keralam ahead of the upcoming Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season. The initiative aims to facilitate the delivery of sacred Swami Prasadam, including Aravana Payasam, to devotees at their doorsteps through Speed Post Parcel service. Pilgrims can book the prasadam at Sannidhanam and have it delivered to their home addresses.

 

The special booking counter will function alongside the Devaswom Aravana and Appam counters at Sabarimala Sannidhanam. In addition, devotees can book and send Swami Prasadam to destinations across the country through any post office in India. The initiative is expected to make prasadam delivery more convenient and ease the difficulties faced by devotees during the pilgrimage season, particularly amid the heavy rush. The Sabarimala temple will open on the 16th of this month for the annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season.

item.title: India issues emergency travel certificate to stranded seafarer in Iran for return home
item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: The Ministry of External Affairs has reiterated that the safety and well-being of Indian seafarers abroad remain a top priority for the government. Briefing media in New Delhi yesterday, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said an emergency travel certificate has been issued to Indian seafarer Akshay Harish from Keralam who was stranded at Chabahar Port in […]
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of External Affairs has reiterated that the safety and well-being of Indian seafarers abroad remain a top priority for the government. Briefing media in New Delhi yesterday, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said an emergency travel certificate has been issued to Indian seafarer Akshay Harish from Keralam who was stranded at Chabahar Port in Iran, paving the way for his early return to India.
 
The seafarer was left stranded in Iran after being informed that his passport and Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC), essential documents for mariners, had been lost while he was aboard a merchant vessel. The MEA spokesperson said the Indian Embassy in Tehran and the Consulate in Bandar Abbas had reached out to him and were coordinating with the ship’s owner, agent and employer to complete the necessary documentation.
 
With the emergency certificate now issued, the government is making all efforts, in coordination with his employer, to ensure his earliest possible return to his home state of Keralam.

item.title: India seeks positive, forward-looking ties with Bangladesh under structured mechanisms, says MEA
item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: Ministry of External Affairs has said that India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh. To a question on the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue, MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal during a media briefing in New Delhi said that, accordingly, initiatives have been taken and meetings held under structured mechanisms in areas such as […]
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of External Affairs has said that India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh. To a question on the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue, MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal during a media briefing in New Delhi said that, accordingly, initiatives have been taken and meetings held under structured mechanisms in areas such as trade, railways, water resources and border management, among others. He said the next round of the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue, which will also take up matters relating to revised travel arrangements, will be held on a mutually convenient date. Mr Jaiswal added that India remains ready to discuss all matters and bilateral issues with Bangladesh through these existing mechanisms, including at the technical level. 
 
The Spokesperson reiterated that the well-being and safety of the Indian seafarers is of high importance to India. He informed that an emergency travel certificate has been issued to Akshay Harish, an Indian seafarer from Keralam who was stranded at Chabahar Port in Iran, paving the way for his earliest possible return home. The Indian seafarer has been left stranded in Iran without a passport or travel documents following a series of disruptions involving his shipping vessel, regional conflict, and missing paperwork.
 
Mr Jaiswal said, India has extended invitations to several  nations, including member states of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), for the upcoming Civilisational Dialogue Forum, scheduled to be held in New Delhi from 20th to 22nd of this month.
 
Responding to a media query, the Spokesperson said that preparations are underway for the event in the national capital, underscoring India’s readiness to welcome participating delegations. 
 
Mr Jaiswal informed that the 19th edition of the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas will be held in Kolkata from 7th to 9th January next year and both the Prime Minister and the President are scheduled to participate in the event.
 
The Spokesperson said, India had participated in the FATF plenary meeting and working group meetings which were held in Paris. He said, FATF, discusses several issues pertaining to illicit financing and India participated in these meetings with the idea to strengthen global networks which try to prevent money laundering, financing of terror, financing of proliferation, and such matters.

item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: In Keralam, the draft electoral roll prepared as part of the Special Summary Revision (SSR) has been published today. A total of two crore 73 lakh 60 thousand and 254 voters have been included in the draft list. Of these, one crore 40 lakh 38 thousand and 718 are women while one crore 33 […]
item.content:encoded:
In Keralam, the draft electoral roll prepared as part of the Special Summary Revision (SSR) has been published today. A total of two crore 73 lakh 60 thousand and 254 voters have been included in the draft list. Of these, one crore 40 lakh 38 thousand and 718 are women while one crore 33 lakh 21 thousand and 267 are men and 269 are transgender voters. The list also includes two lakh 70 thousand and 675 voters in the 18-19 age group and two 45 lakh and 883 overseas voters. 
 
Claims and objections regarding the draft electoral roll can be submitted from today until December 11. The final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027.

Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days. Similar weather conditions are expected over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, […]
item.content:encoded:
India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange colour warning for heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms over Jammu and Kashmir today.

Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days. Similar weather conditions are expected over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for the day. IMD has advised fishermen to avoid venturing into the Andaman Sea till the 16th of this month. Meanwhile, air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Very Poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 321 as of 7 AM today.

item.content:encoded:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands today. The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura today. Similar conditions are expected over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep till tomorrow. 
 
IMD has advised fishermen to avoid venturing into the Andaman Sea until Sunday, and also to stay away from the southeastern Bay of Bengal between the 13th and 15th of this month.
 
Meanwhile, the Weather Agency has forecast a partly cloudy sky along with mist and shallow fog at most places in Delhi during the morning hours today. The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 299 as of 7 AM today.
